title: Inference Rhythm: microbenchmark harness for tokens/sec and p95 regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Build and maintain a lightweight, reproducible microbenchmark harness ("inference rhythm") that measures per-model tokens/sec and p95 tail latency across common payload shapes and caching states. This harness will be the canonical source for day-to-day regression detection and automated alerts tied to our CI and observability dashboards. Goals: 1) Consistently measure tokens/sec (steady-state & microburst), p95 latency, and p99 noise across model family variants; 2) Factor in KV cache warm/cold states and batching; 3) Provide deterministic inputs and synthetic clients for CI, nightly runs, and ad-hoc investigation; 4) Integrate with alerts (PagerDuty-suppression-friendly) and a dashboard with historical baselines and drift detection; 5) Keep runtime overhead minimal so it can be run frequently in pre-prod and nightly suites.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a 5-minute steady-state job per model and emit: tokens_per_sec, p50, p95, p99, CPU/GPU util, median_batch_size
Results stored in metrics DB (Prometheus + long-term TSDB) with tags: model, quantization, batch_config, cache_state, region

Daily/nightly job produced and compared against baseline; regressions (>=10% drop in tokens/sec or >=15% increase in p95 sustained over 3 runs) create an automated issue and annotate the model dashboard
Dashboard tile in Console with 90/95/99th percentiles and tokens/sec trend linking to raw run artifacts
Playbook documented for investigating regressions (links to Confluence doc) and a lightweight local runner for devs to reproduce issues on-demand
implementation_notes: Design the harness as a small Go binary used by CI or a Kubernetes job; reuse existing microbench harness code patterns from ENG-5931 but keep interface smaller and deterministic
Input shapes: short-chat (32 tokens), medium-completion (128 tokens), long-context (1024 tokens) — run with cache cold/warm; synthetic prompt set stored in S3 (rev-controlled)
Measure steady-state: ramp to target QPS, run 5m at target, capture per-request timings and per-token compute where available
Inject model-variant metadata (fp16, int8, quantized) so we can compare across families; tie to model registry name/version
Use Prometheus + Grafana for short-term, push results to ClickHouse for historical baselines and drift analysis
Alert thresholds are conservative to reduce noise: require regression to persist in 3 consecutive nightly runs before auto-page; create slack channel notifications for first detection
tasks: ENG-55013: scaffold harness repo, CI pipeline, and a Docker image for nightly runs
ENG-55014: implement metric ingestion and dashboard panels + regression detector job
Integrate with model-registry tags and ensure run metadata is attached to results
Write Confluence playbook: runbook + troubleshooting checklist
Add unit/integration tests and lightweight local runner for dev reproduction
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy measurements due to infra jitter — Mitigation: run 3 repeated trials and use trimmed-mean; schedule jobs on reserved small pools during nightly windows
Risk: false positives for p95 when model warm-up varies — Mitigation: enforce warm-up phase and explicit cache-state tagging
Risk: storage cost for detailed traces — Mitigation: aggregate by minute for long-term retention and retain full traces for 7 days only

notes: We intentionally keep the harness lightweight so product and solutions engineers can run it in customer investigations without needing cluster access.
Avoid coupling the harness too tightly to CI test infra; support both GitHub Actions and a k8s job template for flexibility.
Regression detector should create a Git issue with embedded run links and a short summary: delta%, affected models, likely cause tags (cache|quant|kernel|infra).
